name: Toyota MR2 (SW20)
h1: Toyota MR2 SW20 (1991–1995): specs, 3S-GTE turbo engine and what owners say

nhtsa.note: NHTSA files every MR2 under MR2, so the 1991–1995 counts cover both the non-turbo car and the Turbo, hardtop and T-top alike.

us.x: Sold new in the US for model years 1991 to 1995, as the non-turbo MR2 (2.2-liter 5S-FE) and the MR2 Turbo (2.0-liter 3S-GTE). Canadian sales ended after 1993. Japan kept building it until August 1999.

fame.x: With its mid-engine layout and looks often compared to the Ferrari 348, the SW20 was nicknamed the baby Ferrari or poor man’s Ferrari.

The SW20 is known for snap oversteer, and CarThrottle says it was called the widow maker. For 1993 Toyota revised the rear suspension, with longer rear toe links and wider 15-inch tires, to cut rear-end breakaway in hard corners.

In 1998 the #25 Team Taisan Jr. with Tsuchiya MR2 won the Japanese GT Championship’s GT300 drivers’ and teams’ titles, winning a record five of the six races held. An MR2 won both GT300 titles again in 1999.
The 3S-GTE takes more boost well. CarThrottle says the stock turbo can give roughly 280 to 300 bhp on a safe 1 bar of boost, and a fully built engine about 350 to 400 bhp.

related.t: Toyota Supra Mk4, its bigger sibling

gens.tag: Mid-engine, rear-drive. 2.0-liter 3S-GTE turbo with 200 hp in the US Turbo; 2.2-liter 5S-FE in the base car. US 1991–1995; Japan built it until August 1999.

variants.name: MR2 Turbo (US)

tq.note: lb-ft at 3,200 rpm; CarThrottle says 203 lb-ft

trans.note: manual only, with a stronger gearbox than the non-turbo car; a viscous limited-slip differential from 1993 (an option per Wikipedia, standard on 1993-on US cars per CarThrottle)

variants.what: The 3S-GTE turbo with an air-to-air intercooler, manual only. 1993 brought the revised rear suspension, 15-inch wheels and bigger brakes; 1994 brought round taillights and a one-piece rear wing.

variants.name: MR2 (US, non-turbo)

tq.note: lb-ft at 4,400 rpm, 1991–92; 145 lb-ft from 1993 (Wikipedia; Consumer Guide lists 140–145)

variants.what: A 2.2-liter twin-cam four shared with the Celica GT and GT-S. It was the only MR2 you could get with an automatic (4-speed); the Turbo was manual only.

variants.name: MR2 GT-S (Japan)

hp.note: 245 PS at 6,000 rpm from Rev 3 (late 1993); early cars 221–225 PS depending on the source (JDM)

variants.what: Japan’s turbo model. From Rev 3 (late 1993) its 3S-GTE got bigger 550cc injectors in place of 440cc and was rated 245 PS. Never sold new in the US.

3S-GTE.name: Toyota 3S-GTE
facts: Inline-4, DOHC 16-valve, air-to-air intercooler (side-mounted in the MR2)
200 hp at 6,000 rpm, 200 lb-ft at 3,200 rpm in the US MR2 Turbo; 245 PS (242 hp) in later Japanese MR2s
1,998 cc, 86 x 86 mm bore x stroke, 8.8:1 compression (1990–93)
CT26 with a twin-entry turbine housing; a revised CT20b from the 1994 model year
Non-interference; CarThrottle says change the belt about every 60,000 miles

issues.x: CarThrottle calls the turbo a major sore point: engine-bay heat shortens its life, and non-synthetic oil can coke the turbo bearing. Its buyer’s guides say to check for blue or white smoke at start-up and under boost, and smoke from the dipstick tube.
issues.fix: Use synthetic oil and idle about three minutes after hard driving, as Toyota recommends.

issues.rx: overheat|coolant (leak|hose)|heater hose|hose from hell|head gasket|air (pocket|in the (cooling|coolant))
issues.x: CarThrottle says the long cooling system is hard to bleed, and trapped air can cause overheating and a blown head gasket. A coolant hose near the exhaust manifold, nicknamed the hose from hell, can burst around 100,000 miles, and overheating on boost can point to a cracked block.
issues.fix: Have the coolant flushed and bled by someone who knows the car.

issues.x: CarThrottle names the cam cover, distributor O-rings and head gasket as common oil leaks, and says a leak can kill the alternator, which is hard to reach in the tight engine bay.
On the MR2 Turbo the catalyst is built into the turbo downpipe, and CarThrottle says long high-speed running can damage it.

5S-FE.name: Toyota 5S-FE
facts: Inline-4, DOHC 16-valve, mounted transversely behind the cockpit

issues.x: CarThrottle names the cam cover, distributor O-rings and head gasket as common SW20 oil leaks, and says a leak can kill the alternator.
CarThrottle says the copper heater pipes that run over the fuel tank tend to crack at their brackets, and replacing them means dropping the fuel tank.
